problem: In speaker-follower VLN data augmentation (Speaker-Follower, EnvDrop), the speaker is trained once with MLE and then frozen during back-translation. The instructions it generates are therefore never optimized for how useful they are to the follower's learning.
motivation: Speaker-augmented data is used throughout VLN, yet nearly all prior work improves the follower and leaves speaker quality underexplored. The resulting follower parameters depend on the speaker parameters, θ_F*(θ_S), but existing methods ignore this dependency. The speaker's real purpose is to make the follower better at following human instructions, so its training signal should come from the follower's loss on human-labeled data.
key_idea: Treat the speaker as a meta-learner in a bi-level optimization (in the style of Meta Pseudo Labels). After each follower update on speaker-generated instructions, the speaker is updated with a REINFORCE-like gradient whose reward is the similarity between the follower's gradients on labeled data and on augmented data.
insight: Rewarding the speaker by gradient alignment between augmented and labeled data adapts generated instructions to the follower's current learning state. The Table 4 ablation shows the bi-level loss and the straight-through reconstruction loss are complementary. Removing reconstruction drops R2R val-unseen SR from 61.6 to 60.2, and removing bi-level drops it to 60.7. Table 3 isolates the speaker's contribution: swapping the EnvDrop speaker for the FOAM speaker while keeping the FOAM follower raises val-unseen SR from 66.0 to 66.5 with pre-exploration and from 70.6 to 72.1 with beam search. The FOAM speaker also produces longer, less truncated instructions with slightly higher BLEU/BERTScore. The benefit depends on having a reasonable speaker to begin with: on RxR the baseline speaker reaches only 7.4 BLEU on English validation, and gains are marginal.
method: Base speaker-follower (EnvDrop reimplementation): LSTM follower pre-trained with imitation + reinforcement learning and LSTM speaker pre-trained with MLE (80k steps on R2R, 200k on RxR). Uses environmental dropout during back-translation and frozen CLIP-ViT-224/16 visual features instead of ResNet.

Back-translation augmentation: the speaker generates instructions for the 176,776 routes EnvDrop randomly sampled from seen training environments. The follower is trained on these synthetic pairs with cross-entropy loss L_u.
Bi-level objective: min_{θ_S} L_l(θ_F*(θ_S)) where θ_F*(θ_S) = argmin_{θ_F} L_u(θ_F, θ_S). The speaker is judged by the follower's supervised loss L_l on labeled human instruction-route pairs.

One-step approximation with alternating updates: the follower takes one SGD step on a speaker-generated batch. The speaker then updates with gradient −[∇_{θ_F} L_l(θ_F^t)ᵀ ∇_{θ_F} L_u(θ_F^{t−1}, θ_S^{t−1})] ∇_{θ_S} log P(î|r̂; θ_S). This is effectively REINFORCE with the cosine similarity of the two follower gradients as reward, derived under a Markov assumption and Monte Carlo approximation.

End-to-end reconstruction loss: the gradient of L_u with respect to the speaker parameters is computed through the sampled instructions with a straight-through estimator and weighted the same way. It is combined with the bi-level gradient to form the final speaker update.
Training schedule: after pre-training, joint follower/speaker training continues to 300k iterations, taking about 3 days on 1 V100. Results are from a single run.

setting.backbone: LSTM follower + LSTM speaker (EnvDrop architecture, trained) on frozen CLIP-ViT-B/16 (224) image features

results: On R2R, FOAM-CLIP-ViT reaches 61.6 SR / 55.1 SPL on val-unseen and 62.2 SR / 56.2 SPL on test. This beats the authors' stronger EnvDrop-CLIP-ViT reimplementation (59.2 / 52.4 on val-unseen; 60.0 / 53.9 on test) by 2.2 SR on test, and also beats earlier ResNet methods (AuxRN, RelGraph, EnvDrop-CLIP-ResNet 59.2 test SR). With beam search it reaches 72.2 test SR, comparable to the large-scale pre-trained VLN-BERT (73), and 68.4 with pre-exploration. On RxR, gains over EnvDrop are marginal: 42.8 vs 42.4 SR on English val-unseen and a tie at 41.2 SR on test.
limitations: Gains largely disappear on RxR's long instructions, where the speaker is weak (7.4 BLEU on English val). The method depends on a reasonably good base speaker.
Updating the speaker online from follower feedback adds training cost: about 3 days on a V100 per run, with extra gradient computations per step.
Evaluation is limited to LSTM-based EnvDrop models on R2R/RxR, with single-run results and small margins. It was not tested with transformer or pre-trained VLN agents or on other datasets.
